bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 Operating Margin Hits 7-Year Low; Valuation at 90x EBITDA
bullets.body: Tesla's Q2 2026 operating margin collapsed to 1.4%, a 7-year low and far below the S&P 500 average of 16-17%. Gross margin fell 420bps sequentially from 21.1% to 16.8%, with Q1 inflated by one-time items. Stock-based comp of $1.15B nearly offset the $1.15B in non-GAAP shareholder earnings, while the stock still trades at a staggering 90x LTM EBITDA—far above the 15-20x threshold considered 'very expensive.' Shares hit session lows down 6.1%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: First-Ever Negative Free Cash Flow Quarter; AI CapEx Scrutiny Intensifies
bullets.body: Alphabet recorded negative free cash flow for the first time in company history (at least since 2016), reflecting the scale of AI capital investment. Stock fell 3.5-5% in premarket after EPS missed excluding Anthropic equity gains. Offsetting positives: Google Cloud revenue surged 82% YoY with operating margin tripling to 35.6% from 20.7%, and GCP is growing faster than the cloud market overall. Wedbush added Alphabet to its best ideas list; WSJ Heard on the Street argued the stock still has upside.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $94B SpaceX Stake Disclosed Post-IPO; $80B Subject to Near-Term Lockup
bullets.body: Google disclosed it holds approximately $94 billion in SpaceX shares following the IPO, with roughly $80B of that position subject to a short-term lockup expiration. The disclosure adds a notable balance sheet variable as markets assess Alphabet's capital allocation amid negative FCF.

bullets.title: GOOGL: EU Hits Google with $1B Antitrust Fine
bullets.body: Google was fined $1 billion by EU regulators for breaking antitrust rules, adding a fresh regulatory headwind to the ad business alongside ongoing AI capex scrutiny.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler CapEx Under Fire as FCF Declines; Markets Demand Revenue Payoff
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit commentators flagging that hyperscalers are transitioning 'from cash-producing machines to capital-intensive operations,' with one noting >$50B/quarter capex requires visible growth to justify. Alphabet's negative FCF quarter seen as the clearest example. Broader concern: 60% of active mutual fund Q2 holdings were AI-related, meaning non-AI funds face massive underperformance risk if the capex narrative holds—but downside risk is sharp if payoffs disappoint.

bullets.title: NOW: Strong 2Q26 Beat—cRPO +21.5% YoY, Operating Margin 300bps Above Guide
bullets.body: ServiceNow delivered a clean 2Q26 beat: cRPO grew 21.5% YoY constant currency (200bps above guidance), subscription revenue grew 23% YoY cc (150bps above high-end guide), and operating margin of 29.5% came in 300bps above guidance. Full-year guide seen as conservative/restrained, likely reflecting pull-forward dynamics.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos Pushes Prime Video AI Overhaul; Alexa Redesigned Away from Anthropic
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos is reportedly directing Prime Video to make AI central to its service redesign. Separately, Amazon has redesigned Alexa to rely less on Anthropic's models, signaling a shift toward proprietary AI dependency reduction across its consumer products.

bullets.title: NVDA: Chinese Open-Source AI Proliferation Reinforces GPU Dominance
bullets.body: One fintwit account argued that despite concerns about Chinese AI competition, Chinese open-source models are trained on NVIDIA GPUs—meaning proliferation of Chinese open-source AI actually reinforces NVDA's dominance rather than threatening it.

bullets.title: UAE to Import High-End US AI Chips 'Very Soon'—Demand Tailwind for Semis
bullets.body: UAE's trade minister stated the country will import high-end AI chips from the US 'very soon,' potentially opening a new geopolitical export channel for US semiconductor makers. UAE also reaffirmed its $1.4 trillion US investment pledge is ahead of schedule.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: Buy the Dip in Memory Stocks
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley recommended buying the dip in memory stocks, a notable call given the broader risk-off environment and rising yield headwinds facing growth equities.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Peacock Turns Profitable for First Time; Q2 EPS Beat
bullets.body: Comcast Q2 delivered a broad beat: adj EPS $1.04 vs $0.97 est, total revenue $29.94B vs $29.3B est, and wireless net adds of 448k vs 384k est. Most notably, Peacock achieved first-ever profitability with adj EBITDA of $189M vs $38M estimate, and Peacock revenue of $1.90B beat $1.76B est.

bullets.title: Oil Surges Past $90 WTI, Brent Near $100 on Houthi Tanker Attacks
bullets.body: WTI crude crossed $90/bbl for the first time since June 11, up ~4%, while Brent approached $100 following Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. Murban futures spiked 26% to $112.56/bbl. RBC's commodities chief warned 'war entering dangerous phase' with oil potentially exceeding 2008 peak levels. Hedgeye confirmed TRADE and TREND breakout signal for WTI.

bullets.title: Global Bond Yields Surge: US 10Y at 4.69%, 2Y at 4.32%, Germany 10Y at 3.2%
bullets.body: US 10-year Treasury yield hit a year-to-date high of 4.69% while the 2-year reached 4.32%. Germany's 10-year touched 3.2% for the first time in over 15 years. UK 5-year at 5.10%. One macro commentator attributed the move to higher oil prices, mounting inflation fears, and anticipated massive sovereign bond issuance competing with debt-hungry hyperscalers—with 'bond vigilantes quietly reasserting influence.' US 30-year real yields near 3%, highest since 2008.

bullets.title: Market Pricing In At Least One Fed Rate Hike by December
bullets.body: Rate futures are now pricing in at least one Fed rate hike by December, a notable hawkish shift amid surging oil prices and inflation concerns. Asset managers' VIX futures positioning has simultaneously fallen to the 1st percentile, signaling extreme complacency at a moment of rising macro risk.

bullets.title: Mortgage Applications Rise 1.9% but 30-Year Rate Climbs to 6.7%—Highest Since Aug 2023
bullets.body: MBA mortgage applications for the week ended July 17 rose 1.9% after a -2.7% prior week, but the 30-year mortgage rate climbed to 6.7%, the highest since August 2023, limiting the housing demand recovery narrative.

bullets.title: Consumer Stress Signal: 25%+ of Working-Age Credit Card Users Can't Repay Grocery Bills
bullets.body: More than 25% of US working-age adults who used credit cards to cover grocery purchases could not repay bills in full, a tangible indicator of elevated consumer debt stress and potential headwind for discretionary spending.

bullets.title: China Credit-Fiscal Impulse Signals Risk of Negative Growth Surprises Ahead
bullets.body: BCA Research notes China's combined credit and fiscal impulse—described as the strongest leading indicator of Chinese economic activity—is currently signaling increased risk of negative growth surprises ahead.

bullets.title: DeepSeek CEO: TileLang to Rapidly Lower CUDA Ecosystem Barriers
bullets.body: DeepSeek CEO Wenfeng stated that advancements such as TileLang 'are expected to rapidly lower barriers to entry created by the CUDA ecosystem,' a notable competitive signal for NVIDIA's software moat even as Chinese open-source model proliferation boosts GPU demand.

bullets.title: AI Narrative Carries 2Q Earnings Season; 60% of Active Fund Holdings Are AI Plays
bullets.body: Fintwit broadly framing 2Q earnings as an AI capex story, with one commentator noting 60% of active mutual fund Q2 holdings were AI-related. Non-AI positioned funds face redemption risk on underperformance. Alphabet and Tesla seen as the headline data points for the capex narrative, even as Alphabet's negative FCF raises questions about returns timing.
